page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16-lssd is an arm64-based server instance powered by 16 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 1608 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The processor features a 1.0 thread-per-core topology without hyperthreading, backed by 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 80 MB L3 cache.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory performance, with the PassMark memory score placing in the top 10% tier. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks show strong read and write speeds of 314.24 GB/sec and 120.6 GB/sec respectively, both ranking in the top 25%. Computational benchmarks reveal average single-core and multi-core performance under stress-ng, while data decompression and compression tasks, such as single-threaded gzip and multi-threaded bzip3, demonstrate strong top-25% execution speeds.

The instance lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX, AVX512, and AMX, and does not support hardware virtualization flags. However, its combination of dedicated ARM cores, top-tier memory performance, and 1608 GB of local NVMe storage makes it highly efficient for database operations, which scored in the top 25% in PassMark testing. It is suited for static web serving, local database hosting, and memory-intensive data processing workloads that benefit from high-speed local storage and strong memory bandwidth.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16-lssd is an arm64 server featuring 16 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture clocked at 3.0 GHz. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory and 1608 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Lacking hyperthreading and x86 vector extensions like AVX-512, the instance instead relies on dedicated single-threaded core performance and an 80 MB L3 cache. Benchmark results highlight top-tier memory performance, with PassMark memory scores in the top 10% and strong large-block memory bandwidth. Database operations and static web serving throughput also rank in the top 25%. This hardware profile offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for storage-heavy and memory-dependent workloads. It is suited for database hosting, web serving, and localized data processing tasks requiring fast local storage and high memory throughput.
